short: Tangent-space covariance + RVM (M06) is new to imagined-speech EEG but a cited motor-imagery pipeline; gains are not uniform and later grouped-CV work finds non-speech confounds.
position: The paper changes one component, the decoder (M06): CSP-filtered EEG as covariance matrices, mapped to tangent space and classified by a multiclass RVM [@nguyen2018inferring]. None of the 5 prior scalp-EEG imagined-speech decoders used Riemannian features (Appendix), but the pipeline is the Riemannian BCI approach the authors cite (§6.2), and its advantage is not uniform: two of 12 Tangent+RVM comparisons are not significant (Table 4) and RVM trails ELM on short-versus-long (§6.1), so M06 is standard. Evaluation (M12) is the period's usual within-subject random cross-validation with a stated, untested chance level, also standard. The strongest confound is non-speech information: the analysed interval contains the word-specific visual cue (§4.1), and a [later] re-analysis of the released data attributes the best contrast to muscle tension and that cue and reports lower accuracy when segments of one trial share a fold [@tates2026unpacking]. The released dataset is the durable contribution; the robustness and word-complexity claims are not supported.
